summary: Gone 100-ft timber tower on Porcupine Ridge, Thurston County, WA; built 1937, WWII Aircraft Warning post, removed or destroyed about 1968; now inside a Weyerhaeuser tree farm, permit required.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS names the Washington Division of Forestry/DNR as administrator, and Forest Lookouts names the state Division of Forestry. Willhite places the summit inside Weyerhaeuser's Vail Tree Farm, where a permit is required. The story reports the register's administration and the permit requirement and does not say who owns the summit.

FFLOS says the structures were removed about 1968; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed about 1968. All three date the end to about 1968, so the story reports the difference without picking one.
FFLOS calls the site Porcupine Mountain; Willhite and Forest Lookouts call it Porcupine Ridge. The story uses both names.

corrections.why: Willhite says a Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm permit is required, and a motorized permit reaches just below the site.

sources.title: Porcupine Ridge Lookout - Weyerhaeuser Tree Farm

notes_for_editor: Built 1937 and removal about 1968 agree across sources; the removed-vs-destroyed wording differs. The brief's access 'unknown' is corrected to permission (Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm). The brief's name Porcupine Mountain is the FFLOS name; Willhite and Forest Lookouts call the summit Porcupine Ridge. Do not confuse this with the Porcupine Ridge lookouts in Montana and Oregon that show up in search results; none were used. The 1952 and 1964 newspaper items come from Forest Lookouts' transcriptions and were not checked against the original papers. Willhite's visit date is not given. Private names from the newspaper items are left out of the story and the evidence quotes.
